heard: A black hole shoots plasma jets at half light speed. Discovered in 1964, Cygnus X-1 is history's first confirmed black hole. It sits 7,000 light years away in the constellation Cygnus. The beast pairs with a blue supergiant star named HDE 226 868. They orbit each other every 5.6 days. The black hole continuously strips material into an accretion disk. These jets shine with the energy of 10,000 suns. Stellar winds make the plasma jets visibly dance and wobble. That explains why a black hole shoots plasma jets at half light speed.
